doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Link Chamberlain's record and Kikuchi's Japanese Miles-inspired date
summary: They recall playing on Link Chamberlain's leader date and Masabumi Kikuchi's On the Corner-style record, part of his run of Japanese dates.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Lighten Up, Please! we’ve talked about with Pee Wee Ellis. Here’s an interesting one, the one with Link Chamberlain that Muse put out, with you and Link and Lyn Christie.
It’s Link’s record. That was Link’s record at a leader. It was his record to lead. We played a Wayne tune there.
And Bob Leonard, who was the first good drummer I ever played with.
He’s from Connecticut. He became – John Stowell is still friends with him.
I don’t remember him at all.
He became a mailman or something.
I have absolutely no memory of him.

First – I played a session. When I was a kid in college, I played a session with him and – with Stowell and Bob Leonard. They were Connecticut buddies. He did – he was a good drummer. Next is a date with Masabumi Kikuchi in New York for East Wind with Hino and Grossman and Reggie – Reggie Lucas, Anthony Jackson, Al Foster, and Ntume.
Because it was a Miles thing. That’s On the Corner. You know the Japs – Japanese.
Imitation is the sincerest form of flattery.
Kikuchi, he’s first generation that. That was definitely that. That was when I started to do a lot of Japanese dates. I was hot in Japan for a minute, a couple of records, Japan.
